ideas.description: Exploit, following E004's contingency. On the current incumbent (E006: subset whitening, max-autotune compile, fp16, channels_last), widen the last group from 576 to 768 channels (128/384/768). Set epochs to 9.25 and stretch the triangular LR to match. Everything else stays fixed: lr 9.0, wd 0.012, ls 0.3, Lookahead, alternating flip, batch 1024 with drop_last. Warm up the new shapes in build. Log ms/step.
ideas.expected: Accuracy 0.752-0.758, centred near 0.755. This comes from E004's 0.7389 at 7.5 epochs plus ~1 pp per epoch over 1.75 epochs, minus a little for diminishing returns. Time ~8.8-9.0 s: about 444 steps at ~20.1 ms/step with max-autotune, plus ~0.06 s prepare. If accuracy is >=0.753, this is the first feasible incumbent; next, step down 0.25 epochs at a time. If it lands at 0.750-0.753, go to 9.5 epochs.

ideas.description: Exploit and probe the width frontier. Widen the last group further to 1024 (128/384/1024) and cut epochs to 8.5, with the LR schedule rescaled and everything else held at the incumbent. Group 3 runs at 8x8 and 4x4, where E004 showed widening is nearly free per step, so this tests whether extra width still buys sample efficiency.
ideas.expected: Per-step time ~21-22.5 ms (+5-10% over 768, not FLOP-proportional). With 408 steps that gives a time of ~8.7-9.2 s. Accuracy 0.750-0.758. If it matches the 768 / 9.25-epoch run's accuracy in >=3% less time, the optimum is wider still and 1280 should be tried. If accuracy falls below 768's on the epoch line, 768 is near the knee.

ideas.description: Exploit, cutting per-step cost where it is concentrated. E004's post-mortem found that the high-resolution group-1 layers (32x32 and 16x16) dominate step time. Cut group 1 from 3 convs to 2 (keep the pooling position and the 128 width). Run it on the best 768-wide config (I-768 at 9.25 epochs if that run is kept; otherwise on the incumbent), keeping the same epochs and everything else.
ideas.expected: Per-step time falls 8-15%, saving ~0.7-1.2 s per trial. Accuracy falls 0.3-0.8 pp. The idea is a win if the loss is under ~1 pp per second saved, i.e. the result sits above the epoch line. If so, pair it with +0.5-0.75 epoch to recover feasibility at lower total time.

ideas.description: Explore, as an alternative way to cheapen group 1. Keep 3 convs in group 1 but narrow its width from 128 to 96 channels (96/384/768, or 96/384/576 on the incumbent if the 768 run isn't kept). The whitening conv output and the group-2 input adjust to match. Same epochs, LR rescaled only as airbench's width-independent scaling dictates (unchanged).
ideas.expected: Per-step time -6-12%. Accuracy -0.2 to -0.6 pp. This tells us whether group-1 width or group-1 depth is the cheaper thing to cut. If the accuracy loss per second saved is below ~1 pp/s, it beats adding epochs and should be combined with the winner of the group-1 depth cut.

ideas.description: Explore. On the incumbent config, lower label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2 and change nothing else. This is a decisive test of H1.3.1, which has never been tested.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). H1.3.1 predicts accuracy drops by >=0.2 pp (to <=0.746 on the 576/9.5-epoch incumbent). If accuracy instead rises or stays within 0.1 pp, H1.3.1 is refuted, and ls 0.2 (or a 0.3->0.4 probe) becomes a free knob worth testing on the 768 net.

ideas.description: Explore. Add loss-based data filtering. During the second half of training, keep the per-example loss computed in the forward pass. Each epoch, drop the 25% lowest-loss examples from the previous epoch, so second-half epochs have fewer batches. Batches stay fixed at 1024 with drop_last, so no new shapes appear. The losses are a byproduct of training (no extra forward passes), and the selection runs on the GPU with the trial-seeded generator. Keep the LR schedule defined over the total number of steps.
ideas.expected: Train time -10-13% (about -0.9 to -1.1 s). Accuracy falls by 0.1-0.6 pp. H1.6.1 holds if the fall is <=0.2 pp. Even a 0.3-0.5 pp fall is a net win at the ~1 pp/s exchange rate, if spending the saved time on epochs recovers more than that.

structured_output.summary: No run has met the target yet. The best so far is E006: 128/384/576 at 9.5 epochs, 0.7475 accuracy in 8.76 s. E004 showed that widening the last group is nearly free per step and buys sample efficiency. So the top idea runs 128/384/768 at 9.25 epochs, expected at about 0.755 in about 8.9 s, which should make it the first feasible incumbent. A second idea pushes the last group to 1024 at 8.5 epochs to find where extra width stops paying. Two exploit ideas go after per-step cost in the high-resolution group 1, which E004 identified as the expensive part: one cuts it from 3 convs to 2, the other narrows it from 128 to 96 channels. Each is judged against the ~1 pp per second exchange rate measured in E002. The explore ideas are a decisive label-smoothing 0.2 vs 0.3 test (H1.3.1) and loss-based data filtering (H1.6.1). Queued I007 (Muon) and I008 (progressive resizing) stay, because their hypotheses are still open. I dropped nothing. I left out the random-flip ablation (H1.2.1) and Cutout (H1.3.2) for now: both are expected to lower accuracy and would add information only. The queue now has 8 queued ideas.
